question: According to the review of statin therapy by Khatiwada and Hong, which statement about statin-associated muscle adverse effects is correct?
options: Muscle-related symptoms are the most common side effect; myopathy often raises creatine kinase above ten times the upper limit of normal, and rhabdomyolysis occurs in about 2-3 cases per 100,000 patients per year.
Rhabdomyolysis is the most common side effect, affecting 1 in 1000 to 1 in 10,000 patients each year.
Statin therapy is not associated with muscle symptoms or elevated creatine kinase.
Myopathy is defined by creatine kinase below the upper limit of normal, and rhabdomyolysis affects about 10% of treated patients.
gold_answer: Muscle-related symptoms are the most common side effect; myopathy often raises creatine kinase above ten times the upper limit of normal, and rhabdomyolysis occurs in about 2-3 cases per 100,000 patients per year.
notes: Calibration item. Every passage was checked against PMC10892755 on 2026-11-19. Human verification, independent annotation, and adjudication are required. Option D is an unused distractor; agents 0 and 1 argue different incorrect positions so the item tests evidence-weighted trust rather than simple vote counting.

positions.answer: Rhabdomyolysis is the most common side effect, affecting 1 in 1000 to 1 in 10,000 patients each year.

claims.text: Rhabdomyolysis is the most common side effect associated with statin use.

evidence.text: The most common side effect associated with statin use is muscle-related symptoms.
In the case of rhabdomyolysis, which affects 2–3 cases per 100,000 patients treated annually, this occurrence is notably less common

claims.verdict_rationale: The review names muscle-related symptoms, not rhabdomyolysis, as the most common side effect, and explicitly describes rhabdomyolysis as notably less common at 2–3 cases per 100,000 patients annually.

claims.text: Myopathy is typically accompanied by a significant increase in creatine kinase that frequently exceeds ten times the upper limit of normal.

evidence.text: Myopathy is typically characterized by muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, accompanied by a significant increase in blood creatine kinase (CK) levels, which frequently exceed ten times the upper limit of normal (ULN) in laboratory tests.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that myopathy is accompanied by a significant increase in creatine kinase that frequently exceeds ten times the upper limit of normal.

claims.text: These muscle side effects occurred only in patients taking simvastatin.

evidence.text: Observational and randomized studies suggest that between 1 in 1000 and 1 in 10,000 patients receiving standard statin doses may experience these side effects each year.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives an annual frequency for patients receiving standard statin doses but makes no comparison between individual statin drugs, so it does not establish or refute a restriction to simvastatin.
